He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball|Seton Hall Pirates]]. ==High school career== Rhoden played basketball for [[Baldwin Senior High School (New York)|Baldwin Senior High School]] in [[Baldwin (hamlet), New York|Baldwin, New York]]. As a junior, he averaged 19.5 points and 6.7 rebounds per game. Rhoden led his team to the [[Long Island]] AA championship and was named [[Nassau County, New York|Nassau County]] Player of the Year.{{cite web |last1=Cordova |first1=David |title=Seasonal Work: A Look At Seton Hall Basketball, Part 3 |url=https://davesjoint.net/2018/12/13/seasonal-work-a-look-at-seton-hall-basketball-part-3/ |website=Dave's Joint |access-date=October 13, 2021 |date=December 13, 2018}} He [[reclassification (education)|reclassified]] to the 2018 class and transferred to [[Our Saviour Lutheran School]] in [[The Bronx]].{{cite web |last1=Kramer |first1=Ari |title=Jared Rhoden has multiple offers to play at Division I schools |url=https://www.newsday.com/sports/high-school/boys-basketball/jared-rhoden-has-multiple-offers-to-play-at-division-i-schools-b37060 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170717101241/http://www.newsday.com/sports/high-school/boys-basketball/jared-rhoden-has-multiple-offers-to-play-at-division-i-schools-1.13795338 |url-status=live |archive-date=July 17, 2017 |website=[[Newsday]] |access-date=October 13, 2021 |date=July 11, 2017}} As a senior, Rhoden averaged 29.3 points, seven rebounds and three assists per game, earning All-''[[USA Today]]'' New York First Team honors.{{cite web |title=2017-18 All-USA New York Boys Basketball Team |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2018/2017-18-all-usa-new-york-boys-basketball-team |website=USA Today High School Sports |access-date=October 13, 2021 |date=April 16, 2018}} He competed for the New York Lightning on the [[Amateur Athletic Union]] circuit.{{cite web |last1=Libert |first1=Mike |title=Explosive #'s from Jared Rhoden |url=https://nychoops.rivals.com/news/explosive-s-from-jared-rhoden |website=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] |access-date=October 13, 2021 |date=January 14, 2017}}{{cite web |last1=Carino |first1=Jerry |title=Seton Hall basketball: 2018 wing Jared Rhoden commits |url=https://www.app.com/story/sports/college/2017/10/28/seton-hall-basketball-2018-wing-jared-rhoden-commits/809869001/ |website=[[Asbury Park Press]] |access-date=October 13, 2021 |date=October 28, 2017}} He committed to playing college basketball for [[Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball|Seton Hall]] over offers from [[Saint Louis Billikens men's basketball|Saint Louis]], [[Wichita State Shockers men's basketball|Wichita State]] and [[Penn State Nittany Lions basketball|Penn State]].{{cite web |last1=Novak |first1=Christopher |title=Jared Rhoden commits to Seton Hall |url=https://www.bigeastcoastbias.com/big-east-recruiting/2017/10/28/16564628/jared-rhoden-2018-commits-seton-hall |website=Big East Coast Bias |access-date=October 13, 2021 |date=October 28, 2017}}{{cite web |last1=Pelzman |first1=JP |title=Seton Hall's Jared Rhoden, looking back and looking ahead |url=https://setonhall.rivals.com/news/seton-hall-s-jared-rhoden-looking-back-and-looking-ahead |website=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] |access-date=October 13, 2021 |date=May 26, 2020}} ==College career== Rhoden underwent shoulder surgery before his freshman season at Seton Hall.{{cite web |title=Jared Rhoden 2019 |url=https://setonhall.rivals.com/news/jared-rhoden-2019 |website=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] |access-date=October 13, 2021 |date=April 12, 2019}} As a freshman, he averaged 3.4 points and 2.6 rebounds per game.{{cite web |last1=Zagoria |first1=Adam |title=With postseason looming, meet the Seton Hall supporting cast who must help Myles Powell |url=https://www.nj.com/sports/2020/02/with-postseason-looming-meet-the-seton-hall-supporting-cast-who-must-help-myles-powell.html |website=[[NJ.com]] |access-date=October 13, 2021 |date=February 7, 2020}} He averaged 9.1 points and 6.4 rebounds per game in his sophomore season as a part-time starter.{{cite web |last1=Carino |first1=Jerry |title=Seton Hall basketball preview 2020-21: Underestimate Jared Rhoden, Pirates at your peril |url=https://www.app.com/story/sports/college/2020/11/24/seton-hall-basketball-preview-2020-21-jared-rhoden/6190280002/ |website=[[Asbury Park Press]] |access-date=October 13, 2021 |date=November 24, 2020}} On December 23, 2020, Rhoden posted a season-high 26 points, 12 rebounds and four assists in a 78–67 win against [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]].{{cite web |title=Cale, Rhoden have career games; Seton Hall beats Georgetown |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2020/12/24/cale-rhoden-have-career-games-seton-hall-beats-georgetown/43298807/ |website=[[USA Today]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=October 13, 2021 |date=December 24, 2020}} As a junior, he averaged 14.9 points, 6.7 rebounds, 1.9 assists and 1.2 steals per game. Rhoden was named to the [[Big East Conference|Big East]] All-Tournament Team after averaging 20.5 points and 10.5 rebounds in two games during the [[2021 Big East men's basketball tournament|2021 Big East tournament]].{{cite web |last1=Mickens |first1=Jorie |title=2021 Pirate Player Preview: Jared Rhoden |url=https://www.wsou.net/news/2021pirateplayerpreview-jaredrhoden.cfm |website=[[WSOU]] |access-date=October 13, 2021 |date=July 12, 2021}} On November 22, 2021, he scored a career-high 29 points in a 79–76 loss to [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]].{{cite news |title=Johnson hits game-winning 3, Ohio St. tops No. 21 Seton Hall |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401372020 |access-date=November 22, 2021 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 22, 2021}} Rhoden was named to the First Team [[List of All-Big East Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big East]] as a senior.{{cite news |last1=Zagoria |first1=Adam |title=Seton Hall star Jared Rhoden named All-Big East first team; former N.J. high school stars R.J. Cole, Adama Sanogo make first team |url=https://www.nj.com/setonhall/2022/03/seton-hall-star-jared-rhoden-named-all-big-east-first-team-former-nj-high-school-stars-rj-cole-adama-sanogo-make-first-team.html |access-date=March 10, 2022 |work=[[NJ.com]] |date=March 6, 2022}} ==Professional career== ===College Park Skyhawks (2022)=== After going undrafted in the [[2022 NBA draft]], Rhoden signed with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] on August 3, 2022,{{cite news|title=Trail Blazers' Jared Rhoden: Signs with Blazers|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/trail-blazers-jared-rhoden-signs-with-blazers/amp/|website=CBSSports.com|date=August 2, 2022|access-date=August 3, 2022}} but was waived prior to the start of the season.{{cite news|title= Trail Blazers Waive Isaiah Miller and Jared Rhoden|url= https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-waive-isaiah-miller-and-jared-rhoden|website=NBA.com|access-date=October 16, 2022|date=October 12, 2022}} On November 4, he was named to the opening night roster for the [[College Park Skyhawks]].{{cite web|title=College Park Skyhawks Roster 2022-23|url=https://cpskyhawks.gleague.nba.com/roster|website=NBA.com|date=November 3, 2022|access-date=November 3, 2022}} ===Detroit Pistons / Motor City Cruise (2022–2024)=== On December 26, 2022, Rhoden signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Detroit Pistons]], splitting time with their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Motor City Cruise]].{{cite web|title= Pistons' Jared Rhoden: Signed by Detroit|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/pistons-jared-rhoden-signed-by-detroit/|website=CBSSports.com|date=December 26, 2022|access-date=December 26, 2022}} On July 2, 2023, Rhoden signed another two-way contract with the Pistons,{{cite tweet|title=The @DetroitPistons announced today that the team has signed guards Jared Rhoden and Malcolm Cazalon to two-way contracts. Per team policy, terms of the agreements were not disclosed.|number=1675530509244411904|user=Pistons_PR|date=July 2, 2023|access-date=October 8, 2023}} and joined them for the [[2023 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|title=DETROIT PISTONS 2023 NBA 2K24 SUMMER LEAGUE ROSTER|url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2023/vegas/team/1610612765/pistons|website=NBA.com|access-date=October 8, 2023}} On August 19, 2024, Rhoden signed with the [[Toronto Raptors]],{{cite web|title=RAPTORS SIGN RHODEN|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-sign-rhoden|website=NBA.com|date=August 19, 2024|access-date=August 19, 2024}}{{cite web|title=Toronto Raptors Officially Sign 2-Year NBA Player|url=https://www.si.com/fannation/nba/fastbreak/toronto-raptors-officially-sign-2-year-nba-player-rhoden|website=SI.com|date=August 19, 2024|access-date=August 20, 2024}} but was waived on October 19.{{cite web|title=RAPTORS WAIVE THREE, CONVERT BATTLE TO TWO-WAY CONTRACT|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-waive-three-convert-battle-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=October 19, 2024|access-date=October 19, 2024}} ===Charlotte Hornets / Greensboro Swarm (2024)=== On October 21, 2024, Rhoden was claimed off waivers by the [[Charlotte Hornets]], subsequently converting his deal into a [[two-way contract]].{{cite web|title=Hornets Claim Jared Rhoden Off Waivers|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets-claim-jared-rhoden-off-waivers|website=NBA.com|date=October 21, 2024|access-date=October 21, 2024}} On November 30, he was waived by the Hornets.{{cite web|title=Hornets Waive Jared Rhoden|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets-waive-jared-rhoden|website=NBA.com|date=November 30, 2024|access-date=November 30, 2024}} ===Raptors 905 (2024–2025)=== On December 8, 2024, Rhoden joined [[Raptors 905]].{{cite web|title=RAPTORS 905 SIGN JARED RHODEN|url=https://raptors905.gleague.nba.com/news/raptors-905-sign-jared-rhoden|website=NBA.com|date=December 8, 2024|access-date=December 9, 2024}} ===Toronto Raptors (2025)=== On March 4, 2025, the [[Toronto Raptors]] signed Rhoden to a two-way contract.{{cite web|title=RAPTORS CONVERT ROBINSON AND SIGN RHODEN|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-convert-robinson-and-sign-rhoden}} In his first career start, he led the Raptors to a March 12 win over the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] with a career-high 25 points and 12 rebounds, making four three-pointers and collecting four steals.{{cite web |title=Jared Rhoden's double-double leads Raptors past 76ers in first career start |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nba/article/jared-rhodens-double-double-leads-raptors-past-76ers-in-first-career-start/ |website=Sportsnet.ca |date=March 12, 2025 |access-date=March 22, 2025}}{{Cite web |title=Raptors 118-105 76ers (Mar 12, 2025) Box Score |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore/_/gameId/401705513 |website=ESPN |access-date=March 22, 2025}} In 10 appearances (2 starts) for Toronto during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], Rhoden averaged 11.4 points, 3.8 rebounds, and 1.4 assists. On April 22, it was announced that Rhoden had undergone surgery to repair a torn [[glenoid labrum|labrum]] in his right shoulder.{{Cite web|title=Raptors Two-Way Prospect Undergoes Shoulder Surgery|url=https://www.si.com/nba/raptors/toronto-raptors-say-jared-rhoden-has-undergone-shoulder-surgery|access-date=April 24, 2025|website=si.com|language=en}} On July 1, the Raptors waived Rhoden.{{cite web | last=Adams | first=Luke | title=Raptors Waive Jared Rhoden | website=Hoops Rumors | date=2025-07-01 | url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2025/07/raptors-waive-jared-rhoden.html | access-date=2025-12-07}} The Raptors re-signed Rhoden on September 27.{{cite web|title=Raptors sign Rhoden|url= https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-sign-rhoden-2 |website=NBA.com|date=September 27, 2025|access-date=September 27, 2025}} He was waived again by the team on October 16.{{Cite web|title=Raptors Waive Five Players|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-waive-five-players|access-date=October 23, 2025|website=nba.com|language=en}} ===Paris Basketball (2025–present)=== On November 1, 2025, the [[Paris Basketball]] of the [[LNB Élite]] and [[EuroLeague]] announced Rhoden as a new player.{{Cite web|title=Jared Rhoden joins Paris|url=https://parisbasketball.com/en/2025/11/49588|date=November
